title: Get the two manuals before you cut anything
body: The fan (2012 F36AR, 356 mm opening) and the OutEquip air conditioner: the exact roof opening and how thick a roof each kit clamps across. Your stack from the outside of the steel to the finished ceiling is 2 15/16 in (2 in of rib plus 15/16 in of covering) plus the steel skin.

title: Cut and frame the roof openings
body: Air conditioner 14 1/4 in square at 49 1/2 in from the rear doors and 34 across; fan 14 in square at 13 1/4 and 34 across. Ribs start at 21 3/4, 37 7/8, 58 3/8, 97 3/8, 126 3/8 in (2 3/4 wide), so the openings sit between them: frame each opening, then seal, rust-proof the cut edges and fit the units.

title: Cut and fit the side window
body: The cutout (the slider frame's outline) is 39 11/16 x 22 5/8 in, 101 3/4 to 141 7/16 in from the back and 39 to 61 5/8 in up, over the dinette table (the glass is bigger, 54 3/8 x 29 1/8 in). The opening is already cut and dry-fitted; the glass is not bonded yet. Where the hole really is on the van is not in the plan (the numbers here assume it is centered over the table): measure its edges from the back mark and the floor and type them in the Side window sizes. Then bond the glass in one planned session. It is steel work, so it comes before the insulation and the wiring.

title: Rough in the wiring before anything is covered
body: 12 V DC runs for the fan (up to 2.7 A), the air conditioner (up to 58 A), the 2 ceiling lights and the battery cable; the hot water heater needs about 133 A through the inverter. Decide the battery (280 Ah), inverter and fuses first, since the electrics are still undecided.

title: Insulate between the ribs and in the walls
body: The ribs hang 2 in, so the insulation fits between them without going past the ceiling plane. Keep it clear of the openings' frames and the wiring.

title: Lay the subfloor
body: Everything else stands on it: the gear cabinet, the couch frame, the counter, the tanks and the battery.

title: Fit the furring strips and the blocking
body: The eight horizontal strips on each wall (1x4 boards laid flat, 3/4 x 3 1/2 in, centered at 3, 12, 21 1/4, 30 1/4, 43 1/2, 57 1/4, 66, 76 3/4 in up, at most 13 3/4 in apart center to center; each sits on spacer blocks 1 1/2 along the wall x 3 1/2 up and 3 5/8 out, or on the steel; S7 stops at the sliding door opening and only S8 carries over it), On the driver side S5 and S6 stop at a four-piece frame around the side window, and the dinette outlet sits at 34 in up under it; then the blocking for the ceiling slats. Do the ceiling blocking before the walls.

title: Cover the ceiling, then the walls
body: Ceiling: 3 sheets of 3/16 in plywood and 15 cedar slats 3 x 3/4 in, the lights on the slats. Walls: 3/8 in birch plywood standing floor to ceiling, joints at 42, 90 and 138 in. Seal both faces and finish before hanging (clear water-based finish or hardwax oil), glue to every strip, a screw with a finish washer about every 8 in, 1/16 in between sheets; then cover the corners and the cut edges with trim and edge banding (the Walls page of the build guide).

title: Build the heavy low things first
body: The battery (21 x 10 in, 52 to 73 in from the back), the hot water tank (87 1/4 to 101 1/4 in) and the fresh water tank (87 1/4 to 122 1/4 in), then the gear cabinet (two floor-mounted panels, the shelf as its sliding top), the removable couch frame on its wall blocks and the deck lid, the counter and the drawers under it. The shower pan (bought, 36 x 24 in) is bedded over its drain hole and fill-tested, then the stall wall and W3 are lined with the thin FRP panel (the Shower pan page of the build guide).

title: Last: wall cabinets, closet and the fold-out table
body: The walls lean in about 5 degrees above 41 5/16 in, so the wall cabinets (63 to 74 9/16 in up) stand 1 15/16 in off the wall at the bottom and 2 15/16 in at the top: scribe the backs or fill the wedge, and cut their tops to the finished ceiling at the wall (74 9/16 in, because the roof arcs up toward the middle). These are the pieces most likely to need small adjustments, so fit them last.
